passage:
Class 10 B group chat
Hrithik: ok can we all agree the new physics sir is the WORST teacher in this school
Hrithik: boring voice, too much homework, total waste
Pankaj: idk i kind of like him
Pankaj: he explained circuits better than anyone
Neelam: same, his numericals finally make sense to me
Hrithik: what?? everyone was complaining yesterday
Pankaj: you were complaining. we were just listening
Hrithik: wow ok so now it's all of you vs me
Neelam: nobody's against you 😅 we just don't agree
Hrithik put his phone face down on the bed. His face was burning.
Hrithik: whatever

qa.q: What does Pankaj say the new physics teacher explained well?
qa.a: Circuits.

qa.q: Why did Hrithik think everyone would agree?
qa.a: He heard complaining the day before and took it as everyone's view, and his own strong dislike made it feel obvious to all.

qa.q: How could Hrithik have opened the conversation differently?
qa.a: He could ask what everyone thinks of the new physics sir before declaring it, and remember that disagreement isn't an attack.

qa.q: How might Neelam feel when Hrithik says it's all of them against him?
qa.a: Neelam might feel misread and a bit uncomfortable, having only shared a different opinion. 😅

grounding: It shows a teenage boy assuming his group shares his opinion of a teacher, speaking bluntly, and feeling attacked when they disagree.

passage:
On the local bus from Nashik Road to their kasba, Wasim was loud as usual. "That new singer from the TV contest, the one with the long braid? Total fake. Can't sing, just cries on stage. Everyone knows that."
Devika, squeezed next to the window, turned sharply. "I voted for her. Twice."
"Come on. Seriously?"
"My whole family watches for her. She sings old Marathi songs properly."
Suresh, from the seat behind, added, "My mother likes her too."
Wasim felt his neck go warm. "Why is everyone jumping on me? I'm just saying what's true."
"You're saying what you think," Devika said. "That's different."
He stared out at the sugarcane fields for the rest of the ride, not sure whether he was angry or embarrassed.

qa.q: How many times did Devika vote for the singer?
qa.a: Twice.

qa.q: Why does Wasim feel everyone is jumping on him?
qa.a: Wasim feels defensive because he believed his opinion was simply the truth everyone shared, so hearing others disagree felt like an attack rather than a normal difference.

qa.q: What could Wasim do next time he wants to share a strong opinion?
qa.a: Say it as his own view, like "I don't enjoy her singing", and ask what others think before calling it a fact.

qa.q: How might Devika have felt hearing her favourite singer called a fake?
qa.a: She might feel stung, since the singer means something to her whole family, so she pushed back.

grounding: It shows a teenage boy assuming everyone shares his view of a TV singer, speaking bluntly, and feeling attacked by disagreement.

passage:
In the corridor of their school in Madrid, Santiago slammed his locker. "Señora Ruiz is the worst teacher this school has ever had. She makes us act out every scene. It's embarrassing." He looked round, waiting for nods.
Kofi shifted his bag. "I actually like her class. It's the only one where I talk."
"You're joking."
"No. And Lucía said drama is her favourite subject."
Santiago felt heat rise up his neck. He had been so sure everyone groaned the way he did. "Great, so you're all on her side."
"It's not sides," Kofi said. "You just hate acting. That's fine."
Santiago walked to maths alone, going over it. He'd said "everyone" as if it were obvious. Maybe it had only been obvious to him.

qa.q: What does Señora Ruiz make the class do?
qa.a: Act out every scene.

qa.q: What does the heat rising up Santiago's neck suggest?
qa.a: He feels embarrassed and a bit defensive, because he had been sure everyone felt the way he did.

qa.q: What went wrong, and what could Santiago try next time?
qa.a: He presented his dislike as everyone's view; next time he could say he finds her class embarrassing and ask how others find it.

qa.q: What is Señora Ruiz's class like for Kofi?
qa.a: It's the only class where Kofi talks, so it matters to him, which is why he gently disagrees.

grounding: It shows a teenage boy assuming his friends share his view of a teacher, speaking bluntly, and feeling ganged up on when they don't.

passage:
In the school bus bay after the Wednesday assembly, Anirudh, fifteen, dropped his bag on the bench. "That new sports teacher is useless. Can't even blow a whistle properly. Everyone thinks so."
Lakshmi looked up from her phone. "I don't. She fixed my running start in two days."
"Come on, Lakshmi. She's so slow. Sangeeta, tell her."
Sangeeta shook her head. "I like her. She lets us choose teams instead of always the captains."
Anirudh's face went hot. "Wow. Okay. So now I'm the bad guy?"
"Nobody said that," Lakshmi said.
"You're both ganging up on me." He pulled his earphones in and turned toward the window, still sure that most of the class agreed with him and these two were just being difficult.

qa.q: What did Lakshmi say the sports teacher fixed?
qa.a: Her running start, in two days.

qa.q: How does Anirudh feel when Lakshmi and Sangeeta disagree, and why?
qa.a: Anirudh feels attacked and embarrassed, his face going hot, because he was sure everyone agreed with him, so their different views feel like ganging up.

qa.q: What could Anirudh do differently when he brings up a teacher he dislikes?
qa.a: He could share it as his own view and ask what others think, instead of saying "Everyone thinks so", which makes disagreement feel like a fight.

qa.q: How might Sangeeta see Anirudh's reaction?
qa.a: Sangeeta may feel puzzled that a simple opinion about choosing teams turned into Anirudh calling himself "the bad guy".

grounding: It shows a teenager assuming everyone shares his opinion about a teacher, speaking bluntly, and feeling attacked when friends disagree.

passage:
Hi Usha di,
Something weird happened at debate club and I need someone sane to tell your little brother he's right.
We had a free session, so I said what I think about that singer from the new talent show, the one everyone's sharing. I said, "Let's be honest, we all know she can't sing, it's just the sad backstory." I thought everyone would laugh and agree. Honestly, I've never met a single person who likes her.
Instead Tanmay said she's the best voice he's heard in years. Three girls said I was being mean. Even Sir said I should "argue, not announce".
I felt like the whole room turned on me. I was only saying what everybody thinks. Or I thought everybody thinks. Maybe my friends just all think like me?
Anyway. Write back. You're on my side, right?
Vishal

qa.q: What did Sir tell Vishal at debate club?
qa.a: Sir said Vishal should "argue, not announce".

qa.q: Why did Vishal expect everyone to laugh and agree?
qa.a: Vishal had never met anyone who liked the singer, so it felt like everyone shared the same view, and the blunt comment seemed safe.

qa.q: What turning point appears in the letter, and what could Vishal do with it?
qa.a: The line "Maybe my friends just all think like me?" is the turning point; Vishal could follow it by asking people outside his usual group what they think before speaking for everyone.

qa.q: How might Tanmay have felt hearing Vishal's comment?
qa.a: Tanmay may have felt dismissed, since "we all know" left no room for someone who truly loves the singer's voice.

grounding: It shows a teenager assuming everyone shares his opinion of a celebrity, speaking bluntly, and feeling the room turned on him when others disagreed.
